While centralized training architectures can alleviate these issues, they often incur poor scalability and increased coordination complexity. This paper introduces CRUISE (Curriculum-structured Reinforcement Learning via Iterative Self-Play), a training framework designed to stabilize independent deep reinforcement learning without employing centralized critics, joint policies, or explicit inter-agent communication. CRUISE structures the learning process through a progressive difficulty curriculum combined with iterative selfplay, enabling decentralized agents to break non-stationary cyclic behaviors (limit cycles) and acquire robust competitive strategies in otherwise unstable learning settings. Ablation studies further confirm that the curriculum structure is the critical factor enabling convergence, rather than policy architecture or reward design.
